blocks.content: The Standard Meridian of India passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh and is taken as the standard time for the entire country.

rows: Run East-West parallel to the Equator
Run North-South converging at the Poles
Determines local time and time zones
Decreases from the Equator to the Poles
All meridians are equal in length

items: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5° N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
The Earth rotates 15° in 1 hour, meaning a difference of 1° longitude equals a 4-minute difference in local time.
The International Date Line roughly follows the 180° meridian, where crossing westward gains a day and crossing eastward loses a day.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Latitudes are imaginary horizontal lines parallel to the Equator measuring distance North or South.
Longitudes are imaginary vertical lines extending from pole to pole measuring distance East or West of the Prime Meridian.
The Equator (0°) divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
The Prime Meridian (0°) passes through Greenwich, London, and serves as the baseline for global time zones.
India's Standard Time (IST) is based on the 82.5° E meridian, placing it 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of GMT.
